title: Why Eid Is the Last Holiday Still Announced Late
seoTitle: Why Eid Is the Last Holiday Still Announced Late
excerpt: Almost every holiday on Oman's 2026 calendar was fixed before the year began. Only two dates still wait on a man looking at the sky, and they are the two that can empty your roster overnight.
seoDescription: Oman now publishes most public holidays a year ahead, except Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. Here is how moon sighting works and how to roster around it.
topic: Why Oman's Holidays Are Announced So Close to the Day

blocks.text: In December 2025, Oman's Cabinet decided that most public holidays would stop being a surprise, publishing Accession Day, Isra and Mi'raj, Islamic New Year and the Prophet's birthday for the whole year in advance. Only two dates on the calendar still wait on someone looking at the sky: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. Those are the two that can empty a hotel roster or a clinic's call desk with barely a day's notice.
A Cabinet decision that changed the calendar

segments.text: For years, every religious holiday in Oman carried the same uncertainty. You knew roughly when Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Islamic New Year or the Prophet's birthday would fall, but the exact day only became official a day or two before it happened. That made rosters, marketing calendars and even school terms hard to lock down months out.

The Council of Ministers changed that at the end of 2025. It approved a policy to publish national and religious holiday dates for the whole Gregorian year in advance, instead of confirming each one as it arrived. The 2026 list came out with Accession Day, Isra and Mi'raj, Islamic New Year and the Prophet's birthday already dated months ahead. The stated reason: help government offices and private businesses plan their schedules and stop holidays colliding with other events on the calendar.

blocks.text: How moon sighting still decides two dates

segments.text: The policy carved out one exception on purpose: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. Both still follow the declarations of the Main Committee for Determining the Start of Hijri Months, chaired by the Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs. The committee meets each month to check whether the new crescent has actually been seen, not calculated from a chart.

Here is the part that explains everything. Most Islamic-calendar holidays fall well into a month whose start was already confirmed weeks earlier. Isra and Mi'raj lands on the 27th night of Rajab. The Prophet's birthday lands on the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal. By the time either date arrives, nobody is guessing anymore. Eid, though, is the first day of a new month, Shawwal or Dhul Hijjah. The sighting decision and the holiday are the same event, which is why Eid can only ever be confirmed a day or two ahead.

blocks.text: Out of Oman's entire public holiday calendar, only two dates still depend on someone looking at the sky, and they are the two that can empty a roster overnight.

segments.text: Here is what a business already knows for the rest of 2026, and what it still does not.

items.text: Isra and Mi'raj: Sunday, 18 January (already passed)
Islamic New Year: Thursday, 18 June (already passed)
Prophet Muhammad's birthday (Mawlid): Thursday, 27 August (already passed)
National Day: Wednesday and Thursday, 25 to 26 November (fixed, still ahead)

segments.text: National Day in November is the only fixed date still ahead of you this year, and it can go straight into the roster now.
Mawlid, back in August, already showed how far ahead a fixed Hijri date can be rostered.

Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha do not work this way. Future dates are only estimates until the sighting committee confirms them, likely within a day or two of each holiday. That window, not National Day, is where a business's planning actually gets tested.

segments.text: Treat your holiday calendar as two separate lists. The fixed list, National Day still ahead this year, and Accession Day, Isra and Mi'raj, Islamic New Year and Mawlid already behind you this year, can go straight into your roster software and marketing calendar today. Nobody needs to check back.

The moon-sighting list needs a different plan. As soon as Ramadan's start is announced, pencil in a window for Eid al-Fitr, and do the same for Eid al-Adha a couple of months later. Decide now who approves overtime, who updates the phone greeting, and who checks the website and WhatsApp hours. Agree the agency rate and the approval chain in advance, so nobody is negotiating at eight in the evening the night the crescent is sighted.

This is also where automation earns its keep. Platforms such as CustomerCare.OM, built to answer Oman's phone lines directly, can update a greeting and posted hours the moment a holiday is confirmed, instead of waiting for someone to rerecord an IVR message on short notice.

blocks.title: Your two-minute check
paragraphs: Pull up Oman's official 2026 holiday list and mark each date fixed or pending.
For the next Eid window, decide today who approves overtime and who updates your greeting message.
Pre-write your phone, WhatsApp and website holiday message with a blank left for the date.
Check your HR file for how holiday pay works for staff asked to work that day.

items.q: Why can't Eid be fixed in advance like National Day?
items.a: Because Eid falls on the first day of a new Hijri month, and Oman confirms a new month by actually sighting the crescent moon, not by calculation alone.

items.q: How much warning do businesses usually get before Eid?
items.a: Typically a day or two. The Main Committee for Determining the Start of Hijri Months meets on the 29th night of the current month and announces its decision that evening.

items.q: Do the other Islamic holidays ever move?
items.a: They can shift by a day if a month's start is confirmed later than expected, but because dates like Mawlid fall well into the month, the date published at the start of the year almost always holds.

items.q: What if staff are asked to work on a public holiday?
items.a: Oman's labour law entitles them to time off in lieu or extra pay. Check your current HR circular for the exact terms before the holiday, not after.

segments.text: Oman did not remove the uncertainty from its holiday calendar. It shrank it to two dates a year. Put the fixed dates on autopilot, and put a real plan behind the two that still depend on the sky. That is the difference between scrambling every Eid and simply confirming a plan you already made.
